item.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
item.description:

Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. item.title: Next-Generation Segmentation in Radiotherapy: A Narrative Review from Atlas-Based Methods to Agentic Vision-Language Models
item.description:
arXiv Query: search_query=all:"foundation model" AND all:medical AND all:segmen… · score 0.47

Precise segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk is an essential prerequisite for modern, high-precision radiation therapy. However, this task has traditionally been time-consuming and subject to high interobserver variability. Motivated by these limitations, more advanced and novel approaches to automating this task have been developed over the past two decades. This narrative review highlights representative milestones, with a focus on the most recent developments. These approaches include atlas-based label propagation, convolutional architectures, promptable foundation models, and…
